Since Directive 73/239/EEC was introduced in 1973, more elaborate risk management systems developed. Solvency II reflects new risk management practices

evidence_text: The "Solvency I" Directive was aimed at revising and updating the current EU Solvency regime. Solvency II has a much wider scope.
mechanism: The need to revise and update the EU Solvency regime led to the creation of Solvency II with a wider scope.

evidence_text: Pillar 1 consists of the quantitative requirements. The pillar 1 framework set out qualitative and quantitative requirements

Technical provisions are divided on claim provisions, pertaining to earned business and premium provisions, pertaining to unearned business. Premium provisions are not equal to unearned premium reserve.
The value of technical provision should be equal to the sum of best estimate of the liabilities and risk margin. The best estimate corresponds to the probability-weighted average of future cash-flows

The best estimate corresponds to the probability-weighted average of future cash-flows, taking into account the time value of money. Usage of central actuarial estimate is required and no margin for prudence is allowed.
Usage of central actuarial estimate is required and no margin for prudence is allowed. no margin for prudence is allowed.
Only cash-flows that are within contract boundaries are taken into consideration. Solvency II specifies exact rules for determination of these contract boundaries.
mechanism: The need to consider only cash-flows within contract boundaries leads to the specification of rules for determining these boundaries.

evidence_text: The SCR is the capital required to ensure that the (re)insurance company will be able to meet its obligations over the next 12 months with a probability of at least 99.5%. In addition to the SCR capital a Minimum capital requirement (MCR) must be calculated
mechanism: The need to ensure that the (re)insurance company will be able to meet its obligations leads to the calculation of a Minimum capital requirement (MCR).

evidence_text: In addition to the SCR capital a Minimum capital requirement (MCR) must be calculated which represents the threshold below which the national supervisor (regulator) would intervene. The MCR is intended to correspond to an 85% probability of adequacy over a one-year period
mechanism: The need to represent the threshold below which the national supervisor (regulator) would intervene leads to the MCR corresponding to an 85% probability of adequacy.

evidence_text: In addition to the SCR capital a Minimum capital requirement (MCR) must be calculated which represents the threshold below which the national supervisor (regulator) would intervene. The MCR is bounded between 25% and 45% of the SCR.
mechanism: The need to represent the threshold below which the national supervisor (regulator) would intervene leads to the MCR being bounded between 25% and 45% of the SCR.

evidence_text: In addition to the SCR capital a Minimum capital requirement (MCR) must be calculated which represents the threshold below which the national supervisor (regulator) would intervene. For supervisory purposes, the SCR and MCR can be regarded as "soft" and "hard" floors respectively.

For supervisory purposes, the SCR and MCR can be regarded as "soft" and "hard" floors respectively. a regulatory ladder of intervention applies once the capital holding of the (re)insurance undertaking falls below the SCR
mechanism: The SCR and MCR being regarded as "soft" and "hard" floors leads to a regulatory ladder of intervention.

evidence_text: a regulatory ladder of intervention applies once the capital holding of the (re)insurance undertaking falls below the SCR, with the intervention becoming progressively more intense as the capital holding approaches the MCR. The Solvency II Directive provides regional supervisors with a number of discretions to address breaches of the MCR
The demanding nature of Solvency II legislation compared to current regulations has attracted criticism. Complying with the new legislation will impose a complex and significant burden
mechanism: The demanding nature of Solvency II legislation leads to a complex and significant burden.

evidence_text: Solvency II's reliance on risk-free interest rate curves makes insurance capital requirements highly sensitive to the low-for-long interest rate environment. Solvency II creates incentives to reach for yield in illiquid asset classes
mechanism: Sensitivity to the low-for-long interest rate environment creates incentives to reach for yield in illiquid asset classes.

evidence_text: Full Solvency II compliance requires annual expenditure equivalent to 3 to 5 percent of premiums for smaller insurers. Full Solvency II compliance requires annual expenditure equivalent to under 1 percent for large groups

Full Solvency II compliance requires annual expenditure equivalent to 3 to 5 percent of premiums for smaller insurers. The introduction of SNCE proportionality status in Directive (EU) 2025/2 is intended to partially address this concern.
mechanism: High compliance costs for smaller insurers leads to the introduction of SNCE proportionality status.

evidence_text: The introduction of SNCE proportionality status in Directive (EU) 2025/2 is intended to partially address this concern. The EUR 100 million threshold excludes the majority of mid-sized European mutuals that face the highest relative compliance burden.
mechanism: The EUR 100 million threshold limits the effectiveness of SNCE proportionality status in addressing the compliance burden for mid-sized European mutuals.
